The differences are such that they affect the identity of the trade marks when each member of the series is compared to each of the others."},{"ref":"TMM/Part13/7/7/1","quote":"The large difference in the relative size of the words in each trade mark significantly changes the prominence of the shared IDAK, as well as the overall visual impression."}],"answer":"Yes, in principle—the Manual treats some variants with city names or numbers as a valid **series of trade marks** (your “set”). This is Manual practice, not a statement of legislation.

For example, the Manual identifies IDAK SYDNEY STANDARD 1 and IDAK MELBOURNE DELUXE 2 as a valid series for hotel accommodation. It also gives a valid series containing IDAK, IDAK SYDNEY, IDAK SYDNEY 1 and IDAK $500, explaining that differences may include the presence or absence of place-name and number statements. [TMM/Part13/6/6/4]

**It is not automatic:** the marks must resemble each other in material particulars. The Manual gives an invalid IDAK MELBOURNE / IDAK SYDNEY example where differences in relative word size change the prominence of IDAK and the overall visual impression. [TMM/Part13/7/7/1]

The supplied legislation does not contain the statutory series requirements, so these passages support a practice-based explanation, not a complete account of the legislative test."}
